name: Minoxidil
description: Pyrimidine-derived vasodilator: scalp solution or foam, and tablets for high blood pressure

status.usStatus: FDA approved (Rogaine OTC); oral hair off-label

note.lead: Oral use for hair is off-label.
note.text: In a 24-week trial of 90 men, oral minoxidil was not superior to topical on hair density.

bullets: **Direct-acting peripheral vasodilator,** per the tablet label
**Lowers blood pressure** by reducing peripheral vascular resistance
**Extra body hair** seen in about 80% of people on the tablets
**For hair growth,** the mechanism is not established
Oral for hair: one RCT, small open studies

practical.routes: On the scalp (solution, foam); by mouth (tablets)
practical.pharmacokinetics: Tablets: peak within 1 hour; about 90% metabolized (glucuronidation)
practical.soldAs: OTC scalp solution or foam (Rogaine); Rx tablets
practical.monitored: Hair counts, scalp irritation, heart symptoms, swelling

regulatory.text: Topical OTC (1988, 1997); tablets for high BP
Oral use for hair loss is off-label
Topical authorised nationally in EU states

references: Olsen et al., J Am Acad Dermatol, 5% vs 2% topical minoxidil, Sep 2002
Penha et al., JAMA Dermatology, oral vs topical minoxidil, Jun 2024
